incidents.title: Wontumi jailed 20 years over illegal mining at Samreboi
incidents.place: High Court, Accra — concession at Samreboi
incidents.summary: The High Court in Accra sentenced Bernard Antwi Boasiako, Ashanti Regional Chairman of the NPP and known as Chairman Wontumi, to 20 years for assigning mineral rights granted to his company Akonta Mining Limited to two individuals without the Lands Minister's approval. A second 20-year term followed for purposely facilitating an unlicensed mining operation on the Samreboi concession, contrary to section 99(2)(b) of the Minerals and Mining Act 2006 (Act 703) as amended in 2019. The trial ran over twelve months and follows the April 2025 raid on sites linked to the company.

incidents.summary: Two excavators impounded after a coordinated swoop by NAIMOS and the Regional Security Liaison Secretariat. Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene urged the public to keep reporting, calling community tip-offs critical to protecting the reserves.

incidents.title: Savannah Region confiscates at least 18 excavators
incidents.place: Damongo and sites across Savannah Region
incidents.summary: Regional Minister Salisu Be-Awuribe said the machines are now with security agencies and operations will continue. He drew the line clearly: small-scale mining is legal with a licence, environmental compliance, and distance from rivers, reserves and cocoa farms.

incidents.title: Party executives accused of interfering after Kobro Forest raid
incidents.summary: Reports allege that local NDC executives intervened over arrests and the confiscation of excavators following an anti-galamsey raid — the pattern of political protection that critics say blunts enforcement.

incidents.title: Intake readings of 12,000–14,000 NTU on five river basins
incidents.place: Pra, Birim, Ankobra, Tano and Offin intakes
incidents.summary: Ghana Water Company logged turbidity between 12,000 and 14,000 NTU at intake points — against roughly 2,000 NTU that treatment plants were built to handle. Commentators warn the fight is losable on politics rather than technique, with enforcement applied selectively.

incidents.title: Convoy blocked at Nyameadom: six held, including two foreign nationals
incidents.summary: A syndicate fleeing in three pickups was stopped without confrontation. They abandoned their excavator at the site. The River Mankran, once the water supply for the Mankranso area, was left polluted alongside large tracts of farmland.

incidents.title: Night raid on the Oda River corridor: 8 arrested, 4 excavators seized
incidents.summary: NAIMOS and the Blue Water Guards moved from the Manso Adubia base at 22:30 on intelligence about active mining on the Oda riverbank. Three of the four excavators had already had their control boards stripped out — a now-routine tactic to make seized machines worthless.

incidents.title: Cape Three Points crackdown shows the state still has reach
incidents.summary: Cited alongside reclaimed forest reserves as evidence the state retains coercive capacity. The same commentary notes the administration has deployed task forces, repealed L.I. 2462, and introduced excavator tracking and satellite monitoring.

incidents.title: NAIMOS quarterly: 237 arrests, 94 excavators, 87.7% strike rate
incidents.summary: Director of Operations Col. Dominic Buah said most of those arrested were foreign nationals. NAIMOS has begun working with GIISDEC to pull wrecked changfan metalwork out of the Ankobra and repurpose seized pumps through the Ministry of Agriculture.

incidents.title: Forestry Commission says degradation accelerated after military pulled out
incidents.summary: Commission CEO Hugh Brown told journalists that 5,252.9 hectares were lost between 2021 and 2024, and linked the recent surge to the withdrawal of military support from anti-galamsey operations on 1 November, which left rapid response teams under-equipped.

incidents.title: $200,000 to restore one kilometre of river
incidents.summary: The price tag on the Birim pilot, run with the Ghana Atomic Energy Commission, Water Resources Commission and GWCL. Analysts note the figure is dwarfed by the damage already done — and it sets the arithmetic for every kilometre still being mined.

incidents.title: Satellite survey: 8,923.8 hectares of forest reserve mined out
incidents.summary: A national remote-sensing verification by the Forestry Commission found 45 forest reserves and one national park impacted by illegal mining as of 31 December 2024 — an area the Commission compared to roughly 12,500 football pitches.

incidents.title: Oda River Forest Reserve is the worst-hit reserve in the country
incidents.summary: 2,654.8 hectares mined out — the single largest loss recorded in any Ghanaian forest reserve. The Oda River corridor remains an active mining front.

incidents.title: Upper Wassa Forest Reserve: 1,660.4 hectares mined out
incidents.summary: The second most degraded reserve nationally, sitting inside the Western Region's belt of eleven affected reserves.

incidents.title: Apamprama Forest Reserve: 1,366.7 hectares mined out
incidents.summary: Third on the national list. Ashanti alone accounts for 4,948.9 hectares across thirteen reserves.

incidents.title: Western North: 2,195.7 hectares gone across twelve reserves
incidents.summary: The second hardest-hit region in the Forestry Commission survey, covering the Sefwi and Bibiani reserve cluster.

incidents.title: Upper East: 210.7 hectares lost in three reserves
incidents.summary: Evidence that the mining front is no longer only a southern forest problem — the northern gold belt around Talensi is now registering reserve loss.

incidents.title: Bono Region: 136.2 hectares lost in a single reserve
incidents.summary: One reserve carries the region's entire recorded loss in the Forestry Commission survey.

incidents.title: Eastern Region: 56.7 hectares across three reserves
incidents.place: Atewa Range and Birim basin reserves
incidents.summary: Small by area, high by stake — these reserves sit on the headwaters that feed the Birim and Densu.

incidents.title: Central Region: 44.7 hectares of reserve impacted
incidents.summary: Recorded in the same national verification exercise; the Offin corridor remains under pressure.

incidents.title: Savannah Region: 29.5 hectares of reserve impacted
incidents.summary: The smallest regional figure in the survey, but the region has since reported active enforcement against excavator crews.

incidents.title: EPA trials ionic nano copper treatment on the Birim
incidents.summary: EPA chief executive Nana Ama Browne Klutse led a simulation applying a nano-liquid directly to the river surface, with the Ghana Standards Authority and Ghana Water Company. If validated, the agency plans to extend it to the Ankobra, Pra and Offin.

incidents.title: 800 acres replanted with cassia and teak at Nyankumase
incidents.summary: Young cassia and teak now hold ground that illegal mining had stripped bare — the clearest reclamation result yet under the current anti-galamsey drive, and proof that recovery is possible where political will holds.

incidents.title: About 60% of Ghana's water bodies now polluted
incidents.summary: Mercury and cyanide used in unregulated mining have contaminated surface and groundwater. Research links exposure in mining communities to kidney failure, birth defects and cancer.

incidents.title: Samreboi dawn operation: 26 arrested across six sites
incidents.summary: A twelve-hour intelligence-led raid by police and the Forestry Commission on sites linked to Akonta Mining. Six Chinese, two Korean and eighteen Ghanaian nationals were held; eight excavators were hauled out and five more left behind for lack of transport. The case that followed ended in a conviction in July 2026.

incidents.title: Cocoa collapse and contaminated rivers across the mining belt
incidents.place: Pra, Ankobra, Oti, Offin and Birim basins
incidents.summary: Excavators and bulldozers have cut through forest, riverbed and farmland alike. Cocobod output stood at 429,323 tonnes — under 55% of seasonal expectation — with illegal mining the main cause. At Mankurom alone, more than 100,000 acres of cocoa were wiped out.

incidents.title: Parliament raises penalties for illegal mining
incidents.summary: Amendments passed in 2024 lengthened jail terms and increased fines. Since 2017, Operation Vanguard and successor task forces have seized and destroyed mining equipment — with mixed and often reversible results on the ground.
